recipes.name: Kkakdugi (Cubed radish kimchi)
ingredients: ⅔ cup Korean hot pepper flakes (gochugaru)
2 tablespoons minced garlic (about 5 or 6 cloves garlic)
instructions: Peel the radish, rinse it under cold water, and pat it dry. Cut it into ¾- to 1-inch cubes and place them in a large bowl.
Add the kosher salt and sugar, and mix well. Let stand for 30 minutes.
Drain the liquid released from the radish into a small bowl and set it aside. Add the minced garlic, ginger, green onions, fish sauce, hot pepper flakes, and ⅓ cup of the reserved radish liquid.
Mix well until the radish cubes are evenly coated with the seasonings and look juicy.
Transfer the kkakdugi to a glass jar and press it down firmly to remove air pockets between the radish cubes.
You can enjoy the kkakdugi right away or refrigerate it for later.

For fermented kkakdugi, leave it at room temperature for about 1 to 2 days, depending on how warm your kitchen is. When small bubbles appear and it develops a pleasantly sour smell, transfer it to the refrigerator.

2 tablespoons minced garlic (about 5 or 6 cloves garlic)

instruction_sections.text: Peel the radish, rinse it under cold water, and pat it dry.
Cut it into ¾-to 1-inch cubes and place them into a large bowl.
Add salt and sugar, and mix well. Tip: If you like your kkakdugi sweeter, add 1 or more extra tablespoons of sugar.
Drain the liquid released from the radish into a small bowl and set it aside.

Add minced garlic, minced ginger, green onions, fish sauce, hot pepper flakes, and ⅓ cup of the juice from the radish. *tip: The amount of hot pepper flakes you use depends on your taste; use ¼ cup hot pepper flakes for a mild version. For a vegetarian version, replace fish sauce with Korean soup soy sauce.
Mix well until the radish cubes are evenly coated with the seasonings and look juicy.
Transfer the kkakdugi to a glass jar and press it down firmly to remove air pockets between the radish cubes.

You can enjoy the kkakdugi right away or refrigerate it for later. If you prefer fermented kkakdugi, leave it at room temperature for about 1 to 2 days, depending on how warm your kitchen is. When small bubbles appear and it develops a pleasantly sour smell, transfer it to the refrigerator.
